profileNote: Every number here is from a --release binary built in a detached worktree with a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR. No debug timing appears in this record.
host: Contended shared machine. All timings are upper bounds. The central effect measured here is a 4.2 second difference, which is roughly five times the ~900ms host noise band established in generation-profile.json, so the conclusion survives the contention by a wide margin.
purpose: Attribute css_base's 4582ms (67.2% of generation, per generation-profile.json) to the work inside it, and name a single target with the milliseconds it would return.
headlineFindings: The cost is not in the node loop and not in CSS generation at all. 89.1% of css_base::build is ONE setup call: css_state_helpers::fluid_height_paths.

Inside that call, 99.7% is authored_css::has_property, which rebuilds the entire authored-CSS Index from scratch on every invocation and is invoked once per (state x node) - 2586 times for live-r15, scanning 3,626,124 rules in total.

The defect is a one-line wrapper. authored_css.rs:82-84 reads `has_property(node, rules, property) { has_property_indexed(node, &Index::new(rules), property) }`. The indexed variant it delegates to is already public, and css_base.rs:57 already builds exactly such an Index for the loop - the hot call site simply does not use it.

Hoisting the Index out of the loop was MEASURED, not estimated: fluid_height_paths falls 4135ms -> 34ms and whole-generation wall falls 6699ms -> 1835ms, while output stays byte-identical across 5 specs and 615 files.

That single change brings generation to 1835ms against the 3896ms it needed to reach, and brings the end-to-end sum to roughly 2939ms against the 5000ms budget. The budget verdict in end-to-end.json flips from over to under.

The superlinearity reported in capture-size-ceiling.json lives here. Cost is linear in (nodes x rules), and since both grow with page size the term is quadratic in page size. A 19MB spec with zero authored CSS rules costs 3ms; a 15MB spec with 1337 rules costs 2005ms.

premiseCorrections.claim: Instruction 1: css_base::build 'takes a prefix and an optional reuse, which suggests it runs more than once per generation'.
premiseCorrections.finding: PARTLY TRUE IN GENERAL, FALSE FOR THE SUBJECT. Measured call counts by a static counter: live-r15 = 1 call, fluid-r1 = 1, fluid-r5 = 1, review = 2 (prefixes r,s), recreate-output = 3 (prefixes r,s,s). The extra calls come from css_interactions::append, which calls css::build_scoped once per RENDERED interaction. live-r15 - the spec that carries the entire latency budget - has no rendered interactions and therefore exactly ONE call.
premiseCorrections.consequence: There is no repeated call to blame on the budget spec. Per instruction 1, the rest of this task applies to that single dominating call.

premiseCorrections.claim: Instruction 2 hypothesis: 'setup is rebuilt on every call over the WHOLE specification while the loop is guarded by cache.emitted, so repeated calls pay full setup for little marginal output'.
premiseCorrections.finding: REFUTED as stated, but the underlying instinct was right one level down. It cannot be repeated CALLS on live-r15 because there is only one call. The hypothesis is nevertheless correct in structure: a setup step IS being rebuilt per unit over the whole rule set - just per NODE inside fluid_height_paths, not per call of css_base::build. Setup is 4199ms of 4641ms (90.5%) and the loop is 72.9ms (1.6%), so the setup-versus-loop framing was correct even though the mechanism was not.
premiseCorrections.consequence: The fix is not call-level memoisation of css_base setup. It is hoisting Index::new out of the per-node loop inside fluid_height_paths.

premiseCorrections.claim: Instruction 3: 'If most nodes hit the cache, the always-paid path is the target; if few do, the declaration builder is.'
premiseCorrections.finding: NEITHER. The premise assumes the loop is where the time is. The entire loop is 72.9ms - 1.6% of css_base::build. Within it the always-paid path is 2.6ms and the cached declaration builder is 59.7ms, so the emitter dominates the loop, but both are rounding error against 4135ms of fluid_height_paths. Deleting the whole loop, emitter and signature path together, would return 1.6%.
premiseCorrections.consequence: Reported for completeness below, but no loop-level optimisation is worth doing. Measuring the call count and the setup/loop split before drilling into the loop is what prevented this task from optimising 1.6% of the problem.

premiseCorrections.claim: generation-profile.json attributed 4582ms to the phase marker named css_base.
premiseCorrections.finding: CONFIRMED and slightly extended. That marker fires at css_base.rs before append_filtered and append_authored_media, so it understates the FUNCTION. Measured here, css_base::build total is 4641ms median, of which the marker covers setup+loop (4272ms) and the remaining 361ms is the filtered/media tail previously attributed to css_responsive. Both records agree within their spreads.
premiseCorrections.consequence: No correction needed to generation-profile.json. The function's true cost is 4641ms, marginally larger than the marker suggested.

namedTarget.target: authored_css::has_property rebuilding the authored-CSS Index on every call, from the per-node loop in css_state_helpers::fluid_height_paths

defectSites.code: pub fn has_property(node: &Node, rules: &[String], property: &str) -> bool { has_property_indexed(node, &Index::new(rules), property) }
defectSites.problem: Index::new(rules) is O(rules) and is rebuilt on every call.
Called once per node per state, so the O(rules) index construction is multiplied by (states x nodes).

namedTarget.shape: A setup step that is linear in the whole rule set, re-executed once per item. Cost = states x nodes x rules, measured at 1.137 microseconds per rule visit.
namedTarget.proposedFix: Build the Index once per state, outside the node loop, and call the already-public has_property_indexed. No new API is required; both the Index type and the indexed entry point already exist and are already used by css_base.rs:57.

millisecondsReturned.basis: MEASURED, not extrapolated. Implemented behind an env flag in a throwaway worktree and A/B tested against the stock path.

correctnessEvidence.method: Aggregate SHA256 over the per-file SHA256 of every emitted file, sorted by path, compared between the stock and hoisted paths.
correctnessEvidence.semanticInvariants: fluid_height_paths returned authored=84 and result=17 identically in both arms on live-r15.
correctnessEvidence.caveat: Byte-identical output on five specs is strong evidence of a pure refactor but is NOT a substitute for the mutation qualification. This record proposes the change and does not land it.

budgetConsequence.statement: This single change is on its own sufficient to bring the stated end-to-end budget from missed by 2308ms to met with roughly 2061ms of headroom. No other optimisation is required to reach 5000ms.
budgetConsequence.unitsCaveat: The two stages count different units, as end-to-end.json records; 2939 is an upper-bound style sum, not a percentile, and the verdict does not depend on it because generation alone now sits far below the whole budget.

superlinearity.question: capture-size-ceiling.json found generation superlinear in spec size (fitted exponent 1.73 within the synthetic family). Does that superlinearity live in css_base, and in which part?
superlinearity.answer: YES, and specifically in authored_css::has_property inside fluid_height_paths. It is not in the node loop, not in parsing, and not in file writing.
superlinearity.mechanism: has_property cost = calls x rules = (states x nodes) x rules_per_state. Both nodes and authored rules grow with page size, so the term is quadratic in page size. A fitted whole-generation exponent of 1.73 is exactly what a quadratic term diluted by linear parsing and writing terms produces.

evidence.model: hasPropertyMs = k x totalRuleVisits, with totalRuleVisits = sum over calls of rules-per-state

points.note: median of 4 runs; the others are single runs

evidence.fittedK: 1.04 to 1.14 microseconds per rule visit, consistent across two independent specs with different node and rule counts
evidence.decisiveControl: fluid-r5 is a 19.03MB spec with 464 nodes and ZERO authored CSS rules, and costs 3ms. review is a SMALLER 15.05MB spec with 1337 rules and costs 2005ms. Spec bytes therefore do not predict this cost at all; the product of nodes and rules does. This also explains capture-size-ceiling.json's observation that the real-site anchor is more expensive per byte than the synthetic ladder pages: real sites carry authored stylesheets, synthetic ladder pages carry almost none.
evidence.constantVersusSuperlinear: This is a superlinear term, not a large constant. Cost per node is not flat: it rises in proportion to the rule count of the page, so the same fix pays off more on larger pages, and the current behaviour degrades quadratically as pages grow.

instrumentationOverhead.design: Counterbalanced interleaved A/B, 4 pairs, alternating which arm ran first (OFF,ON / ON,OFF / OFF,ON / ON,OFF), so ordering could not be confounded with the treatment.
instrumentationOverhead.separation: Complete. The slowest hoisted run (1943ms) is faster than the fastest stock run (5720ms) by 3777ms, and the sign is consistent in 4 of 4 pairs. There is no overlap between the two distributions, so the effect is not attributable to host noise.
instrumentationOverhead.instrumentedVersusUninstrumented: The stock instrumented median (6699ms) sits within the uninstrumented band recorded in generation-profile.json (10 runs, 5796-6695ms). Instrumentation therefore costs on the order of a few hundred milliseconds against a 4221ms effect, and every figure above is reported from the instrumented binary in BOTH arms so the overhead cancels from the comparison.

additionalFindings.systemicPattern: The rebuild-the-index-per-call shape is not unique to has_property. Every non-indexed convenience wrapper in this area constructs an Index and immediately delegates to its _indexed twin: authored_css.rs:6 (normalize), authored_css.rs:83 (has_property), authored_css.rs:92 (positive_integer_property, test-only), inherited_styles.rs:10, responsive_output.rs:20, responsive_node_rules.rs:28. Only has_property is currently hot, because only it is called from a loop over states x nodes. The others are latent instances of the same defect and would become hot if ever called from a per-node loop.
additionalFindings.ownershipNote: responsive_output.rs and responsive_node_rules.rs are owned by work item 006 per the standing file-ownership list. They are named here as observations only; they were not edited, and nothing in this record requires editing them.
additionalFindings.nextLargestRemaining: With the target fixed, css_base::build falls to 420.5ms, of which append_filtered is 227.4ms (54%). That becomes the largest remaining piece inside css_base, but at 227ms against a 5000ms budget it is not worth pursuing and no work is recommended on it.
